results.name: prefix_extension_yes_change
results.description: For 4-example sets whose first three examples are also shown as a 3-example set, yes rate on the 4-example set minus the 3-example set over the same non-example targets; observed above null means adding a fourth example narrows generalization less (or broadens it more) than the model predicts.
results.code:
# name: prefix_extension_yes_change
# description: For 4-example sets whose first three examples are also shown as a 3-example set, yes rate on the 4-example set minus the 3-example set over the same non-example targets; observed above null means adding a fourth example narrows generalization less (or broadens it more) than the model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    x = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    n = x.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mn = x.min(axis=1)
    mx = x.max(axis=1)
    isin = x.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    nd = x.sub(t, axis=0).abs().min(axis=1)
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    pre = s.where(n == 4).str.rsplit(",", n=1).str[0]
    k = pd.DataFrame({"s": s, "t": t, "r": r, "n": n, "pre": pre, "isin": isin})
    k = k[~k["isin"]]
    three = k[k["n"] == 3].groupby(["s", "t"])["r"].mean().rename("r3").reset_index().rename(columns={"s": "pre"})
    four = k[k["n"] == 4].groupby(["pre", "t"])["r"].mean().rename("r4").reset_index()
    m = four.merge(three, on=["pre", "t"])
    v = (m["r4"] - m["r3"]).mean() if len(m) else 0.0
    return float(0.0 if (v is None or not np.isfinite(v)) else v)

results.name: tight_cluster_outside_near
results.description: For sets of 2+ examples spanning at most 15, yes rate on targets 1-5 outside the span (below min or above max); observed above null means people stretch a tight cluster's range further than the model predicts, below means they stop at the examples' edges.
results.code:
# name: tight_cluster_outside_near
# description: For sets of 2+ examples spanning at most 15, yes rate on targets 1-5 outside the span (below min or above max); observed above null means people stretch a tight cluster's range further than the model predicts, below means they stop at the examples' edges.
def test_statistic(df):
    x = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    n = x.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mn = x.min(axis=1)
    mx = x.max(axis=1)
    isin = x.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    nd = x.sub(t, axis=0).abs().min(axis=1)
    out = ((t > mx) & (t - mx <= 5)) | ((t < mn) & (mn - t <= 5))
    sel = (n >= 2) & ((mx - mn) <= 15) & out
    v = r[sel].mean()
    return float(0.0 if (v is None or not np.isfinite(v)) else v)

results.name: within_item_trial_slope
results.description: Correlation between rating and trial_index after subtracting each (set, target) cell's mean of both; observed below null means the same item gets fewer yes answers later in the session than the time-blind model predicts (a true drift, not stimulus order).
results.code:
# name: within_item_trial_slope
# description: Correlation between rating and trial_index after subtracting each (set, target) cell's mean of both; observed below null means the same item gets fewer yes answers later in the session than the time-blind model predicts (a true drift, not stimulus order).
def test_statistic(df):
    x = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    n = x.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mn = x.min(axis=1)
    mx = x.max(axis=1)
    isin = x.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    nd = x.sub(t, axis=0).abs().min(axis=1)
    key = df["number_set"].astype(str) + "|" + t.astype(str)
    ti = df["trial_index"].astype(float)
    rr = r - r.groupby(key).transform("mean")
    tt = ti - ti.groupby(key).transform("mean")
    v = float((rr * tt).sum() / np.sqrt((rr ** 2).sum() * (tt ** 2).sum()))
    return float(0.0 if (v is None or not np.isfinite(v)) else v)

results.name: plus_minus_ten_minus_nine_eleven
results.description: Yes rate on non-example targets exactly 10 from some example minus those exactly 9 or 11 from some example (and not 10 from any); observed above null means people generalize along same-final-digit neighbours in the next decade more than the model predicts.
results.code:
# name: plus_minus_ten_minus_nine_eleven
# description: Yes rate on non-example targets exactly 10 from some example minus those exactly 9 or 11 from some example (and not 10 from any); observed above null means people generalize along same-final-digit neighbours in the next decade more than the model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    x = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    n = x.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mn = x.min(axis=1)
    mx = x.max(axis=1)
    isin = x.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    nd = x.sub(t, axis=0).abs().min(axis=1)
    dd = x.sub(t, axis=0).abs()
    ten = dd.eq(10).any(axis=1)
    ne = (dd.eq(9) | dd.eq(11)).any(axis=1) & ~ten
    v = r[ten & ~isin].mean() - r[ne & ~isin].mean()
    return float(0.0 if (v is None or not np.isfinite(v)) else v)

results.name: above_minus_below_near
results.description: Yes rate on targets 1-10 above the largest example minus yes rate on targets 1-10 below the smallest example (sets of 2+ examples); observed above null means people favour upward extension of ranges more than the model's upward-room term predicts, below means less.
results.code:
# name: above_minus_below_near
# description: Yes rate on targets 1-10 above the largest example minus yes rate on targets 1-10 below the smallest example (sets of 2+ examples); observed above null means people favour upward extension of ranges more than the model's upward-room term predicts, below means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    x = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    n = x.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mn = x.min(axis=1)
    mx = x.max(axis=1)
    isin = x.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    nd = x.sub(t, axis=0).abs().min(axis=1)
    up = (t > mx) & (t - mx <= 10) & (n >= 2)
    dn = (t < mn) & (mn - t <= 10) & (n >= 2)
    v = r[up].mean() - r[dn].mean()
    return float(0.0 if (v is None or not np.isfinite(v)) else v)

results.name: split_cell_fraction
results.description: Fraction of (set, target) cells with at least 5 answers whose answers are not unanimous; observed above null means people disagree on the same item more than the model's per-item yes probabilities imply (they are too sharp), below means people agree more than predicted.
results.code:
# name: split_cell_fraction
# description: Fraction of (set, target) cells with at least 5 answers whose answers are not unanimous; observed above null means people disagree on the same item more than the model's per-item yes probabilities imply (they are too sharp), below means people agree more than predicted.
def test_statistic(df):
    x = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    n = x.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mn = x.min(axis=1)
    mx = x.max(axis=1)
    isin = x.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    nd = x.sub(t, axis=0).abs().min(axis=1)
    key = df["number_set"].astype(str) + "|" + t.astype(str)
    g = r.groupby(key).agg(["size", "mean"])
    g = g[g["size"] >= 5]
    v = ((g["mean"] > 0) & (g["mean"] < 1)).mean()
    return float(0.0 if (v is None or not np.isfinite(v)) else v)

results.name: shared_multiple_k_far
results.description: For sets of 2+ examples that are all multiples of some k in 3..12, yes rate on non-example targets more than 10 from every example that are multiples of k minus those that are not; observed above null means people extend shared-divisor rules to distant numbers more than the model predicts.
results.code:
# name: shared_multiple_k_far
# description: For sets of 2+ examples that are all multiples of some k in 3..12, yes rate on non-example targets more than 10 from every example that are multiples of k minus those that are not; observed above null means people extend shared-divisor rules to distant numbers more than the model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    x = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    n = x.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mn = x.min(axis=1)
    mx = x.max(axis=1)
    isin = x.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    nd = x.sub(t, axis=0).abs().min(axis=1)
    hit = pd.Series(False, index=df.index)
    use = pd.Series(False, index=df.index)
    for k in range(3, 13):
        allk = ((x % k == 0) | x.isna()).all(axis=1) & (n >= 2)
        use = use | allk
        hit = hit | (allk & (t % k == 0))
    far = (nd > 10) & ~isin & use
    v = r[far & hit].mean() - r[far & ~hit].mean()
    return float(0.0 if (v is None or not np.isfinite(v)) else v)

results.name: far_target_magnitude_corr
results.description: Correlation between target value and rating among non-example targets more than 15 from every example; observed above null means people say yes to distant large numbers more (relative to distant small ones) than the model predicts.
results.code:
# name: far_target_magnitude_corr
# description: Correlation between target value and rating among non-example targets more than 15 from every example; observed above null means people say yes to distant large numbers more (relative to distant small ones) than the model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    x = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    n = x.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mn = x.min(axis=1)
    mx = x.max(axis=1)
    isin = x.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    nd = x.sub(t, axis=0).abs().min(axis=1)
    sel = (nd > 15) & ~isin
    a = t[sel].astype(float)
    b = r[sel]
    v = float(np.corrcoef(a, b)[0, 1]) if sel.sum() > 2 and b.std() > 0 else 0.0
    return float(0.0 if (v is None or not np.isfinite(v)) else v)
